definitions.explanation: Refers to extremely tall buildings, typically exceeding 60 meters (about 20 stories) in height. Also used as a prefix for things at extremely high altitudes.

examples.japanese: {超高層|ちょうこうそう}⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{立|た}ち{並|なら}んで⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Super high-rise buildings stand in a row.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新宿|しんじゅく}→新宿：30634_shinjuku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{超高層|ちょうこうそう}⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many super high-rise condominiums in Shinjuku.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{超高層|ちょうこうそう}⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{地上|ちじょう}→地上：12108_chijou⟧50⟦{階建|かいだ}て→階建て：29226_kaidate⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{展望|てんぼう}→展望：12393_tenbou⟧フロア⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{富士山|ふじさん}→富士山：09514_fujisan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: This super high-rise building has 50 above-ground floors, and you can see Mt. Fuji from the observation floor.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{超|ちょう}→超〜：28619_chou⟧ (ultra-, super-) and ⟦{高層|こうそう}→高層：04145_kousou⟧ (high-rise, upper level). In Japanese architecture, a building is generally classified as {超高層|ちょうこうそう} when it exceeds 60 meters in height (roughly 20 stories). The term became common during Japan's construction boom of the 1970s and is strongly associated with the skyscrapers of ⟦{新宿|しんじゅく}→新宿：30634_shinjuku⟧{副都心|ふくとしん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧ — super high-rise building; skyscraper
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}⟦マンション→マンション：01035_manshon⟧ — super high-rise condominium (tower mansion)
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}⟦{建築|けんちく}→建築：02709_kenchiku⟧ — super high-rise architecture
- {超高層|ちょうこうそう}⟦ホテル→ホテル：01027_hoteru⟧ — super high-rise hotel

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{高層|こうそう}→高層：04145_kousou⟧ — high-rise; high altitude
- ⟦{低層|ていそう}→低層：21924_teisou⟧ — low-rise
- {中層|ちゅうそう} — mid-rise
- ⟦タワーマンション→タワーマンション：28914_tawaamanshon⟧ — tower condominium (colloquially タワマン)
